# Partner Channel Design

Source: https://lowob.com/research/partner-channel-design/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-08-28 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Distribution

> Summary: Most partner programmes are written after the first partners sign, which is why so many partners do nothing. We set out five design decisions to make first: the role partners play in the sale, the partner types that fit it, the economics each needs, what tiers should reward, and the rules of engagement. We draw on how the largest cloud programmes tier partners and on where partner-delivered spend actually sits.

Partner channel design is the set of decisions a firm makes before recruiting partners: what job partners do in the sale, which partner types fit that job, how each is paid, what earns a higher tier, and who owns the customer when two parties touch the same deal. The stakes are large in technology markets: Canalys estimated that 70% of worldwide IT spending in 2025 flowed through partners. Most mid-size programmes skip the design and start with a partner agreement and a logo page. The result is a long list of signed partners and a short list of partner-sourced revenue.

*Figure: Where this piece sits: the commercial line, where the build starts.*

The usual sequence in a 50 to 500 person firm runs backwards. A few partners appear, often through a founder's network. A partner agreement is drafted from a template. A partner page goes up. Only when partners fail to produce pipeline does anyone ask what they were meant to do.

Our earlier piece *Integrators, OEMs and channel partners* covers the partner's side of this: what a partner must believe before it will carry a product, and the stages from recruited to scaling. This piece covers the vendor's side: the five design decisions that should precede recruitment, and how the largest programmes make them.

## Where partners sit in the buying process

The case for partners rests on where buyers already are.

| Finding | Source | Implication for channel design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 70% of IT spending flowed through partners in 2025, down from 71% in 2024 and 73% in 2023 | Canalys, IT spending forecast 2025 | Partners remain the main route, but direct and marketplace routes are gaining share |
| On average 13 people are involved in a business purchase; 89% of purchases span two or more departments | Forrester, State of Business Buying 2024 | Partners often hold relationships with stakeholders the vendor never meets |
| 67% of B2B buyers prefer a rep-free experience | Gartner, March 2026 | Buyers lean on advisers and platforms they already trust |
| B2B marketers use an average of 3.7 sales channels | Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, November 2025 | Channel choices are rarely deliberate; most firms inherit their mix |

The Canalys figures are analyst estimates and are revised over time. The trend matters more than the level. A small decline in partner share each year means partners are not disappearing, but the roles they play are shifting: with more weight on implementing, managing and advising, and some transactions moving to cloud marketplaces (Part 16 of this series).

The Ehrenberg-Bass report *Easy to Find* offers a useful check. If a channel carries 30% of category revenue, a brand should expect roughly 30% of its own revenue there. A firm with almost no partner revenue in a category where most buying runs through integrators has a presence gap, not a product gap.

## Decision one: the role partners play in the sale

The first design decision is the partner's job. Five roles cover most technology programmes, and each implies a different contract.

| Role | What the partner does | Who holds the customer contract | Typical payment | What the vendor must supply | First measure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refer | Introduces a buyer and steps back | Vendor | One-off or time-limited fee on paid revenue | Fast follow-up and visible status | Referred deals reaching paid |
| Influence | Shapes the shortlist or specification, often as adviser | Vendor | Usually none directly; access, co-marketing, certification | Evidence partners can repeat to clients | Deals where the partner was named by the buyer |
| Resell | Buys and resells, owning billing | Partner | Margin between wholesale and resale price | Pricing sheet, deal registration, quoting tools | Partner-sold revenue and renewal rate |
| Deliver | Implements, integrates or manages the product | Usually vendor, with partner services contract | Services revenue the partner bills itself | Training, certification, a support path | Time to go-live; customer retention |
| Embed | Builds the product into its own offering | Partner | Royalty or per-unit fee | Technical integration and roadmap visibility | Units shipped; attach rate |

Most mid-size firms need two of these, not five. A software firm selling to regulated mid-market buyers might pair deliver partners, who implement, with influence partners, the consultants who write the buyer's requirements. Choosing roles first prevents the common mistake of signing resellers in a market where buyers want to contract directly. Our explainer *Affiliate vs partner vs referral* covers where referral schemes and affiliate programmes fit alongside these roles, and Part 15 covers referral partners in detail.

## Decision two: economics that cover the partner's cost of sale

A partner programme is a margin structure before it is a relationship. The test is simple: does the partner make enough from your product to justify the time it takes to sell, implement and support?

Partners count their own costs: the seller's time, presales engineering, certification, the risk of a failed implementation. A reseller margin that looks generous against the vendor's list price may be thin against those costs, especially on a first deal. That is why programmes often reward origination more than fulfilment (AWS's ACE programme, for example, offers discounts to partners for originating new customer opportunities), and why services revenue often matters more to a deliver partner than any fee from the vendor.

An illustrative check, labelled as such: if a deliver partner needs about ten days of consultant time to implement your product and its services rate covers that, the product earns its place. If implementation takes thirty days and customers will only pay for ten, no fee you offer will keep that partner selling. The fix is in the product and the playbook, not the margin.

## Decision three: what tiers should reward

Tiers exist to decide who gets scarce vendor resources: leads, funding, technical support and executive time. The largest cloud programmes show what a tier can reward when it is designed around customer outcomes.

| Programme | Tier structure | What qualifies a partner | What the higher tier opens up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AWS Partner Network, services path | Select, Advanced, Premier | Accredited and certified individuals, and launched customer opportunities: 3 at Select (combined monthly revenue of at least $1,500), 20 at Advanced, 50 at Premier | Marketing development funds from Advanced; Premier requires a partner business plan and executive review, and adds early access to sponsorship packages |
| Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program, Solutions Partner designations | Designation per solution area | A partner capability score of at least 70 of 100 points, with every metric above zero, across performance, skilling and customer success | Designation benefits; separate enterprise and SMB tracks with different thresholds |
| Google Cloud Partner Network, announced December 2025 for rollout in early 2026 | Select, Premier and a new Diamond tier, for all partner types | Joint customer outcomes for tiers; competencies measured on certifications and sales credentials, and on contributions to validated closed/won opportunities | Higher designations; engagements applied automatically toward tier and competency progress |

Two design choices stand out. All three programmes count certified people, which measures whether the partner can deliver. And all three count customer outcomes: launched opportunities at AWS, net customer adds, usage growth and deployments at Microsoft, validated closed/won opportunities at Google Cloud. None tiers on revenue alone.

A mid-size vendor does not need three tiers. Two are usually enough: a registered tier with access to training and deal registration, and a committed tier with joint planning, named support and any marketing funds. The qualifying criteria should be things the vendor can verify from its own records, such as certified staff, customers live and renewed, and partner-sourced pipeline, rather than self-reported revenue.

## Decision four: rules of engagement

Rules of engagement decide what happens when the vendor's sellers and a partner touch the same account. They need to be written before the first joint deal, because the first dispute will set the precedent otherwise.

The minimum set covers four things. **Deal registration:** how a partner claims an opportunity, what evidence is required, and how long the claim lasts. **Account ownership:** which accounts the direct team keeps, and whether partners may work them. **Pricing authority:** who may discount, and how far. **Hand-offs:** what happens to a partner-registered deal the partner cannot progress.

Competition law sets limits on some of these choices. In the EU, Regulation 2022/720, the Vertical Block Exemption Regulation, has applied since 1 June 2022 and runs to 31 May 2034. It decides which restrictions a supplier may place on its distributors and resellers without falling foul of EU competition rules. The Commission's accompanying Guidelines on vertical restraints describe the safe harbour as applying where neither party's market share exceeds 30%. They confirm that resale price maintenance is a hardcore restriction. They also give separate guidance on information exchange where a supplier sells directly in competition with its distributors, which is the position of any vendor running a direct team alongside resellers. Programmes that set partner pricing, allocate territories or run a direct team alongside resellers should have counsel review the rules once, early. Part 19 of this series covers channel conflict in practice.

## Decision five: what gets recorded

Every partner programme generates decisions that later need defending: why a partner was moved up a tier, why a margin changed, why a registered deal was given to the direct team. These belong in the decision record The Build Order describes, with a reason, an owner and an expected outcome (*The commercial decisions worth recording*).

The single measure that matters most is the one our earlier piece recommends: partner-sourced pipeline that reaches a paid outcome, reported monthly beside the direct equivalent. A programme that cannot report it does not yet know whether it works. Our explainer *What is a distribution diagnostic?* describes how to test a partner route before committing a team to it.

> Design the partner's job, pay and rules before you sign the first partner. Otherwise the first partner designs them for you.

Illustrative example: a data platform redesigns its partner channel

Decision
:   Replace a single reseller tier with two roles: deliver partners for implementation and influence partners for advisory firms that write requirements.

Reason and owner
:   Eighteen signed resellers had produced two deals in a year; buyers in the segment preferred to contract directly. Owned by the head of partnerships, agreed with the revenue leader.

What changed
:   Deliver partners were tiered on certified staff and customers live; influence partners received certification and evidence packs, not fees. Partner-sourced pipeline was reported monthly beside direct pipeline.

Illustrative: a composite of a mid-size data platform, built from patterns across engagements.

## lowob takeaways

- **Choose the partner's role first.** Refer, influence, resell, deliver and embed each need a different contract and payment.
- **Pay for the partner's cost of sale.** If implementation costs more than customers will pay, no margin fixes it.
- **Tier on what you can verify.** Certified people and customers live are better criteria than self-reported revenue.
- **Write the rules before the first joint deal.** Registration, ownership, pricing authority and hand-offs set every later precedent.

Gateway card

### Before you recruit the next partner

- One or two partner roles chosen and written down
- The partner's cost of sale estimated for a first deal
- Two tiers defined with criteria you can verify from your own records
- Deal registration, account ownership and pricing authority written
- Partner-sourced pipeline to paid reported monthly beside direct
